info.title: NameGender API
info.summary: Infer gender from names, emails and usernames, with the evidence behind each answer.
info.description:
Every lookup endpoint accepts both GET and POST so it can be called from a browser, a shell or a server. All paths live under `/api/v1`; a future breaking change will get a new version prefix instead of altering these.

**Success and failure.** The HTTP status code is the only success signal: a 200 carries the result, anything else carries the error body described below. There is no separate success flag in the JSON.

**Credits.** One credit per resolved name, not per request: a bulk call for 100 names costs 100 credits. Credits are checked before any work starts, so a request is never half-processed. Free accounts get 100 credits per day.

**Rate limit.** 1200 requests per minute per API key by default, counted per key rather than per IP so that several customers behind one address do not share a bucket. Every response carries `X-RateLimit-Remaining`; a 429 carries `Retry-After`.

**Errors.** Every failure, at every status code, returns the same body shape. Branch on the machine-readable `error` field, never on `message`: messages are translated into 22 languages and their wording can change.

**Support.** Each response carries a `request_id`, also sent as the `X-Request-Id` header. Quote it in any support request and we can find the exact call in our logs. You may send your own `X-Request-Id` to correlate with your tracing system.

**Data version.** Responses include `data_version`, the name-dataset snapshot that produced the answer. If a result changes between two calls, comparing this field is the first thing to check.

post.summary: Upload a file and start processing it
post.description:
Uploads a CSV or XLSX file (up to 100 MB, 1,000,000 rows) and, by default, queues it. One credit per row, reserved when processing begins; a job that fails is not charged.

`name_column` is required unless `start=false`: a guessed column that turns out to be wrong would spend credits on the wrong data. Send `start=false` to get the columns, a preview and the credit cost first, then call `/start`.

If starting fails (no credits, unknown column, AI consent), nothing is left behind: no job, no stored file.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header to retry safely: a repeat with the same key returns the first job with `200` and `Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of opening a second one.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Up to 80 printable ASCII characters, unique per upload. SDKs generate one for you.

file.description: CSV, TSV or XLSX with a header row.

name_column.description: Header of the column holding the names, exactly as written in the file. Required unless `start=false`.

country_column.description: Header of a column holding a country code per row, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or alpha-3 (`FR` or `FRA`, any case). Unrecognised values fall back to `country`.

country.description: Default country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, or alpha-3) for rows without one.

ai_fallback.description: Ask an AI model for names not in the dataset. Requires AI consent on the account, exactly as on /gender/bulk.

best_guess.description: Return the more likely gender even when the evidence is weak.

delete_after_download.description: The result can be downloaded once, then it is deleted.

get.description: Pass a full name or a first name. Titles, punctuation and surnames are stripped before lookup; `name` in the response shows what was actually looked up.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The value to resolve.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 code (alpha-3 such as `ITA` is also accepted and converted). Narrows the lookup to one country, which matters for names that flip gender across borders: Andrea is male in Italy and female in Germany. Omit it and the answer is the worldwide aggregate.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: A language tag such as `de-DE`, `en_US` or `pt_BR.UTF-8`, typically the browser's `navigator.language` or the `Accept-Language` header of your sign-up form. Its region becomes the country when `country` is not sent. A tag without a region (`en`, `de`) sets no country: a language alone does not say which country it is spoken in. `country_source` in the response tells you which one was used.

parameters.name: ip
parameters.description: The end user's IP address (IPv4 or IPv6), for example from your sign-up request. Its country is used when neither `country` nor a `locale` with a region is sent. Private and reserved ranges are ignored. The address is used for this lookup only and is not stored. IP geolocation by DB-IP (db-ip.com), CC BY 4.0.

parameters.name: ai_fallback
parameters.description: Ask a language model when the dataset has no answer. Slower and less certain; the response reports `source: "llm"` so you can tell these apart. Requires AI lookups to be enabled in account settings; otherwise the call fails with `ai_consent_required`.

parameters.name: best_guess
parameters.description: Return the most likely gender even below the confidence threshold, instead of null. Check `probability` before trusting the result.

200.description: Resolved. `gender` is null when the name is not recognised — that is a successful answer of "we do not know", not an error, and it still costs one credit.

get.summary: Which countries a name is recorded in
get.description:
This is not a "country of origin" lookup, and it is deliberately not named like one: the data cannot support that claim, and the difference is measurable.

Counted name statistics exist for eleven countries only: birth registrations in the US, UK, France, Canada, Spain, Ireland, Norway, Austria and Israel, and living-resident counts in Poland and Switzerland. Everything else is presence data — it says a name occurs in a country, not how many people carry it. So a query for `Mehmet` ranks Switzerland and France first, at about 29% each, and Turkey does not appear in the ranking at all, because Turkey publishes no counts.

The response therefore keeps the two apart. `registrations` is measured volume and is comparable, but only among the counting countries. `attested_in` is presence, and that is where Turkey, Japan and India show up. Neither field is a claim about any person's origin or ethnicity.

**Credits.** One credit per request. `ai_fallback` and `best_guess` do not apply here and are ignored.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The first name to look up.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many counted countries to list in `registrations`. Shares and `basis.counted_countries` are not affected, and `attested_in` is never cut.

200.description: Country distribution, with the basis of the numbers stated in the response itself.

basis.note: Shares are calculated only across countries that publish counted name statistics…

get.description:
Says whether a name typed into a sign-up or lead form looks like a real person's name, and why. It catches keyboard mashing ("asdf qwerty"), placeholders ("Test Test", "John Doe", "n/a"), fictional characters ("Mickey Mouse"), profanity, digits, symbols and email addresses in the name field. One credit per name.

**It never calls a name fake.** The answer is an `assessment` (`plausible`, `suspicious` or `implausible`), a `score` from 0 to 100 and the `signals` behind it. Use it to flag a record or ask for more information, not to reject people automatically.

Real names that trip simpler filters are left alone: surnames such as Null, Test or Cockburn, two-letter names such as Ng, single names, and every script we cannot read. A first name found in official birth records raises the score; a name we have never seen does not lower it on its own. Surnames are judged by their shape only, because there is no surname dataset behind this endpoint.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name as typed into the form. Send this or `first_name`/`last_name`.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Country hint, as on the gender endpoints. Used for name parsing and for the record lookup.

200.description: Checked.

get.description:
Turns a name into a salutation line ready for a letter or email: "Sehr geehrte Frau Dr. Müller,", "Sayın Ahmet Bey,", "Madame,", "山田様". The gender lookup is included and the price is the same: one credit per name.

**When the gender is not certain, the salutation is neutral.** A wrong gender is worse than none, so the gendered form is used only when the gender is known with at least `min_probability` (default 90), and the language has what it needs (a surname for "Herr Müller", a given name for "Ahmet Bey"). `form` and `reason` say which form was chosen and why. `best_guess` and `ai_fallback` do not apply here. Companies and role addresses get the language's form for organisations.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Full name, titles included. Send this or `first_name`/`last_name`.

parameters.name: first_name
parameters.description: Given name, when your CRM keeps names in separate fields. No parsing is done.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Email address, used when neither `name` nor `first_name`/`last_name` is sent. The name is read from the part before the @; role addresses such as info@ get the form for organisations. Addresses carry no accents, so anna.mueller@ greets Frau Mueller, not Müller.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: The language the salutation is written in: `en`, `en-US`, `en-GB`, `de`, `de-AT`, `de-CH`, `fr`, `es`, `it`, `pt`, `pt-PT`, `pt-BR`, `nl`, `tr`, `pl`, `ja`. When omitted, the language of `locale`, then the main language of the country, then `en`. An unsupported language is an error, never a silent fall back to English.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Country hint for the gender lookup, as on the gender endpoints. It does not set the language when `language` is sent: write to Mr Müller in the US in English.

parameters.name: gender
parameters.description: Gender you already know. Overrides the lookup; `neutral` always gives the neutral form.

parameters.name: min_probability
parameters.description: Lowest probability for a gendered salutation. Below it the neutral form is used.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Academic title kept in a separate field. Used in German and English salutations.

200.description: Salutation built.

post.description:
`data.object` is the job, exactly as `GET /api/v1/batches/{id}` returns it. `result.url` needs your API key to download.

Answer with any 2xx within 10 seconds, then do the work. Anything else (including a redirect) is retried after 1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 6 h, 12 h, 24 h; after 8 attempts the event is given up. Order is not guaranteed.

parameters.name: NameGender-Signature
parameters.description: `t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>`. `v1` is HMAC-SHA256 of `"<t>.<raw body>"` with the endpoint secret. During a secret rotation a second `v1` is present for 24 hours; accept the request if any `v1` matches. Reject a `t` more than 5 minutes from your clock.

parameters.name: NameGender-Event-Id
parameters.description: Same as `id` in the body, and the same on every retry. Deduplicate on it.

parameters.name: NameGender-Delivery-Attempt
parameters.description: 1 on the first try, then 2, 3… up to 8.

2XX.description: Received. Any 2xx status counts; the body is ignored.

apiKeyHeader.name: X-Api-Key
apiKeyHeader.description: Alternative header form, for clients that cannot set `Authorization`. Keys are never read from the query string or the request body.

Error.description: The one error shape. Returned by every endpoint at every failing status code.

error.description: Machine-readable and stable. **Branch on this.** New codes may be added over time, so treat an unrecognised value as a generic failure rather than crashing.

message.description: Human-readable, translated into the caller's language. Wording can change; never parse or compare it.

docs.description: Link to this error in the documentation.

errors.description: Field-level detail. Present on validation failures only.

retry_after.description: Seconds to wait. Present on 429 only, and mirrored in the `Retry-After` header.

query.description: The input exactly as you sent it.

name.description: The first name actually looked up, after stripping titles and surnames.

first_name.description: Given name parsed from the input. Present even when `gender` is null, and not charged separately. Titles and initials are never returned. For Chinese, Korean and Japanese script the surname comes first in the input and is returned in `last_name`.

middle_name.description: Any further given names between the first name and the surname, for example "Fitzgerald" in "John Fitzgerald Kennedy". Initials are dropped.

last_name.description: Surname parsed from the input, including particles such as "van" or "de la". "Smith, John" is read as surname first. With a Spanish-speaking `country` the last two words are both surnames (Pérez García). Always null for usernames, where a surname cannot be told apart from any other word.

name_type.description: `organization` when the input carries a company marker (Acme LLC, Müller GmbH, Stanford University); `role` for shared mailboxes and placeholder accounts (info@, Customer Service, guest). Both return `gender: null` and no name parts. `personal` means no such marker was found; it does not confirm the input is a real name. null when the input is not a name at all.

gender.description: null means the dataset has no confident answer. This is not an error.

probability.description: Share of people with this name who have the reported gender. 0 when unknown. Measured against held-out data, answers at 80+ come true about 95% of the time, so this number runs slightly conservative rather than optimistic.

sample_size.description: How many real people the answer is based on. A probability of 100 from a sample of 3 is weaker than 85 from a sample of 90,000 — read the two fields together. 0 means the source recorded proportions rather than counts.

country.description: The country the answer came from, when narrowed.

took_ms.description: Whole milliseconds spent resolving this value on our side; network time is not included.

source.description: How the answer was reached. `db` exact match; `script` matched after transliterating a non-Latin script; `fuzzy` closest spelling; `llm` language model; `none` no answer. Use it to decide how much to trust a row.

confidence.description: Sample size bucket: high ≥100 people, medium ≥25, low ≥1, unverified when the source gave proportions instead of counts.

matched_as.description: For `fuzzy` and `script` sources, the dictionary entry that was actually matched. Always inspect this before accepting a fuzzy result.

credits_charged.description: How many credits this call took from the balance: one per value resolved.

credits_remaining.description: Balance once this call is paid for: purchased credits plus whatever is left of today's free quota.

data_version.description: Name-dataset snapshot that produced the answer.

request_id.description: Identifier of this call, also sent as the `X-Request-Id` header. Quote it in support requests.

country_source.description: Where the country came from: the `country` parameter, the region of `locale`, the `ip` address, or none of them (null, worldwide answer).

names.description: The values to resolve, each at most 200 characters. Each one costs one credit.

country.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 code applied to every value in the batch. Alpha-3 is also accepted.

locale.description: Language tag whose region becomes the batch country when `country` is not sent, for example `it-IT`. A tag without a region sets no country.

ip.description: End user IP address whose country becomes the batch country when neither `country` nor a regional `locale` is sent. Not stored. IP geolocation by DB-IP (db-ip.com), CC BY 4.0.

type.description: How to read the values in `names`.

ai_fallback.description: Ask a language model for values the dataset cannot answer. Requires AI lookups to be enabled in account settings; otherwise the batch fails with `ai_consent_required`.

best_guess.description: Return the most likely gender even below the confidence threshold, instead of null. For `email` and `username` batches it applies to the extracted first name.

took_ms.description: Whole milliseconds spent resolving the batch on our side, network time excluded.

country_source.description: Where the country came from: the `country` parameter, the region of `locale`, the `ip` address, or none of them (null, worldwide answer).

results.description: Same order as the names you sent.

CountriesResponse.description: Two lists, deliberately not merged. `registrations` is measured volume and is comparable only among countries that publish counts. `attested_in` is presence, with no weight attached — a country appears there whether or not anyone counted it.

credits_charged.description: How many credits this call took from the balance: always 1.

credits_remaining.description: Balance once this call is paid for.

data_version.description: Name-dataset snapshot that produced the answer.

request_id.description: Identifier of this call, also sent as the `X-Request-Id` header. Quote it in support requests.

took_ms.description: Whole milliseconds spent building the distribution on our side, network time excluded.

name.description: The name that was looked up.

basis.description: What the numbers rest on. Carried in the response rather than left to the documentation, because the person reading a percentage is not reading the docs.

counted_sources.description: The statistical offices that publish observation counts.

counted_countries.description: Countries with counted registrations for this name, before `limit` is applied. Can be larger than the length of `registrations`.

note.description: Plain-language caveat. Show it next to the percentages.

registrations.description: Countries with counted registrations, most first, cut to `limit`. Shares are calculated across every counted country before the cut, so they sum to 100 only when nothing is cut.

share.description: This country's percentage of the name's registrations across all counting countries, including any that `limit` cut from the list.

gender.description: Majority gender for the name in this country.

probability.description: Share, 0–100, carrying that gender in this country.

source.description: Statistical office the count comes from.

attested_in.description: Every country the name occurs in, counted or not, alphabetically.

credits_remaining.description: Purchased credits plus whatever is left of today's free quota.

purchased_credits.description: Paid balance. Credits stay on your balance until you spend them.

free_today.description: Free credits left today. Resets at midnight UTC.

lifetime_requests.description: Requests made with this account so far.

reason.description: Why the neutral form was used. Null for gendered and organisation forms.

neutral.description: The gender-free form, always returned, for your own threshold.

parts.description: Pieces of the formal line, for building your own template.

gender_source.description: `input`: the `gender` parameter. `title`: a courtesy title in the name (Frau, Mr). `lookup`: our dataset.

assessment.description: `implausible`: at least one high-severity signal. `suspicious`: a medium signal or two low ones. Otherwise `plausible`.

score.description: Higher is more like a real name. For your own threshold.

first_name_status.description: `counted`: in official birth statistics. `attested`: recorded without counts. `not_found`: not in our data.

identified.description: Rows given a gender. Set once completed.

reserved.description: Held from the balance when processing began.

charged.description: Final charge. Null until completed; a failed job is not charged.

WebhookEvent.description: Envelope of every webhook request. The raw body is what the signature covers.

type.description: New types can be added. Answer 2xx to a type you do not recognise and ignore it.

credits_remaining.description: Same as `credits_remaining` on `/api/v1/me`: purchased, subscription and today's free credits together.

purchased.description: Purchased credits. They stay on the balance until spent.

subscription.description: Subscription credits left in the current period.

daily_burn.description: Average credits used per day over the last 14 days.

runway_days.description: Days the balance lasts at that rate. `credits.low` only.

since.description: When the condition was first seen.

402.description: Out of credits. Buy more, or wait for the daily free quota to reset at midnight UTC.

403.description: Key or account is not permitted to make this call. Codes: `blocked`, `email_not_verified`, `ip_not_allowed`, `proxy_secret_required`, `forbidden`.

404.description: No endpoint at this path, or no such file job on this account. Codes: `unknown_endpoint`, `batch_not_found`.

405.description: Wrong HTTP method for this endpoint.

409.description: The file job is not in a state that allows this. `status` says what it is. Codes: `batch_not_startable`, `batch_not_finished`, `batch_in_progress`.

410.description: The file job has no result to download any more: it failed, was cancelled, expired, or was a single-download result already fetched.

422.description: Input failed validation. `errors` names the offending fields. Codes: `invalid_input`, `too_many_items`, `ai_consent_required`.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded, or too many file jobs running at once. Wait `retry_after` seconds. Codes: `rate_limited`, `too_many_batches`.

500.description: Unexpected server error. Nothing was charged. Quote `request_id` if it persists.

503.description: The name dataset is being rebuilt. Retry shortly; this is brief and expected during a data refresh.

unknown.summary: Name not in the dataset — a successful "we do not know"

fuzzy.summary: Resolved by closest spelling — note the capped probability
